- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# Salesforce DX Project

Salesforce DX is a development approach that brings source-driven development, team collaboration, and continuous integration to the Salesforce Platform. Instead of working directly in an org through a web browser, you work with metadata as source files in a local DX project, track changes in version control, and deploy through automated processes.

This project template gets you started with the tools and structure you need to build Salesforce applications using source control, scratch orgs, and the Salesforce CLI.

## Prerequisites

Before you start, make sure you have:

- **Salesforce CLI** - Download from [developer.salesforce.com/tools/salesforcecli](https://developer.salesforce.com/tools/salesforcecli). See [Install Salesforce CLI](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_setup.meta/sfdx_setup/sfdx_setup_install_cli.htm) for details.
- **VS Code with Salesforce Extension Pack** - See [Installation Instructions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/sfvscode-extensions/guide/install.html) for details. Includes the Agentforce Vibes extension.
- **A development org** - Sign up for a free Developer Edition org [here](https://developer.salesforce.com/signup).
- **Dev Hub enabled** (optional, required to create scratch orgs) - You can enable Dev Hub in your development org under Setup > Dev Hub. See [Provide Developers Access to Salesforce DX Tools](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_setup_dx_tools.htm).

## Project Structure

Your DX project follows this structure:

- **`force-app/main/default/`** - Your metadata source files live in this default package directory. You can configure additional package directories in the `sfdx-project.json` file.
- **`config/`** - Scratch org definitions and project settings
- **`scripts/`** - Automation scripts for common tasks
- **`sfdx-project.json`** - Project manifest that defines package directories, namespace, API version, and other project-level settings

See [Salesforce DX Project Configuration](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_ws_config.htm).

## Get Started

Ready to start developing? The [Get Started with Salesforce DX](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_get_started_dx.htm) guide walks you through your first project, from creating a scratch org to creating a simple Apex class or LWC to deploying your code to a sandbox.

## Common Salesforce CLI Commands

Here are common CLI commands that you'll use the most:

- `sf org login web`: Authorize an org
- `sf org open`: Open your org in a browser
- `sf org create scratch`: Create a scratch org
- `sf project deploy start`: Deploy metadata to your org
- `sf project retrieve start`: Retrieve metadata from your org
- `sf template generate <artifact>`: Scaffold new components, such as Apex classes and triggers, LWC components, Lightning apps, and more
- `sf apex <command>`: Run Apex tests, run anonymous Apex blocks, and view logs
- `sf data <command>`: Work with test data
- `sf alias <command>`: Manage org aliases
- `sf config <command>`: Configure CLI settings

## Use Agentforce Vibes to Build Lightning Apps

Transform your ideas into custom Lightning apps that extend CRM workflows directly in Lightning Experience. Through natural conversations with Agentforce Vibes, implement custom objects and fields, complex business logic, and dynamic UI components. See [Build a Lightning App Using Agentforce Vibes](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/einstein-for-devs/guide/lexapp-overview.html).

# Salesforce DX Project

Salesforce DX is a development approach that brings source-driven development, team collaboration, and continuous integration to the Salesforce Platform. Instead of working directly in an org through a web browser, you work with metadata as source files in a local DX project, track changes in version control, and deploy through automated processes.

This project template gets you started with the tools and structure you need to build Salesforce applications using source control, scratch orgs, and the Salesforce CLI.

## Prerequisites

Before you start, make sure you have:

- **Salesforce CLI** - Download from [developer.salesforce.com/tools/salesforcecli](https://developer.salesforce.com/tools/salesforcecli). See [Install Salesforce CLI](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_setup.meta/sfdx_setup/sfdx_setup_install_cli.htm) for details.
- **VS Code with Salesforce Extension Pack** - See [Installation Instructions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/sfvscode-extensions/guide/install.html) for details. Includes the Agentforce Vibes extension.
- **A development org** - Sign up for a free Developer Edition org [here](https://developer.salesforce.com/signup).
- **Dev Hub enabled** (optional, required to create scratch orgs) - You can enable Dev Hub in your development org under Setup > Dev Hub. See [Provide Developers Access to Salesforce DX Tools](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_setup_dx_tools.htm).

## Project Structure

Your DX project follows this structure:

- **`force-app/main/default/`** - Your metadata source files live in this default package directory. You can configure additional package directories in the `sfdx-project.json` file.
- **`config/`** - Scratch org definitions and project settings
- **`scripts/`** - Automation scripts for common tasks
- **`sfdx-project.json`** - Project manifest that defines package directories, namespace, API version, and other project-level settings

See [Salesforce DX Project Configuration](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_ws_config.htm).

## Get Started

Ready to start developing? The [Get Started with Salesforce DX](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_get_started_dx.htm) guide walks you through your first project, from creating a scratch org to creating a simple Apex class or LWC to deploying your code to a sandbox.

## Common Salesforce CLI Commands

Here are common CLI commands that you'll use the most:

- `sf org login web`: Authorize an org
- `sf org open`: Open your org in a browser
- `sf org create scratch`: Create a scratch org
- `sf project deploy start`: Deploy metadata to your org
- `sf project retrieve start`: Retrieve metadata from your org
- `sf template generate <artifact>`: Scaffold new components, such as Apex classes and triggers, LWC components, Lightning apps, and more
- `sf apex <command>`: Run Apex tests, run anonymous Apex blocks, and view logs
- `sf data <command>`: Work with test data
- `sf alias <command>`: Manage org aliases
- `sf config <command>`: Configure CLI settings

## Use Agentforce Vibes to Build Lightning Apps

Transform your ideas into custom Lightning apps that extend CRM workflows directly in Lightning Experience. Through natural conversations with Agentforce Vibes, implement custom objects and fields, complex business logic, and dynamic UI components. See [Build a Lightning App Using Agentforce Vibes](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/einstein-for-devs/guide/lexapp-overview.html).

- [Salesforce CLI Installation Guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_setup.meta/sfdx_setup/sfdx_setup_intro.htm)

16	---
17	
18	## 1. Executive Summary
19	
20	Field technicians lose time on-site hunting for the right Asset record — scrolling long lists on a small screen, mistyping serial numbers, or phoning the office. This BRD defines the requirements for a single **Lightning Web Component ("Asset Finder")** that replaces/supplements the mobile Asset list view and lets a technician locate a record in under 10 seconds via **text search, GPS-based nearby search, or barcode/QR scan**, defaulting to **recently viewed** records on open. The component must work fully offline against pre-cached data and must never invoke Apex at runtime.
21	
22	This document covers the business context, process (as-is/to-be), functional and non-functional requirements, the data model as grounded against the target org, business rules, assumptions, risks, and acceptance criteria. It is the input to the Epics/Stories and Solution Design stages that follow.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 2. Business Context
27	
28	Field technicians work across large sites and remote locations with unreliable connectivity. On arrival, they must identify the correct piece of equipment before they can log service activity against it. Today:
29	
30	- The default Salesforce list view is not optimized for mobile search.
31	- It is unusable offline.
32	- Technicians scroll long lists, mistype partial names, or call the office to read a serial number off a physical label.
33	- Digital assets/metadata are inconsistently tagged, and time is lost re-creating records that already exist.
34	
35	**Business impact:** lost technician productivity per site visit, avoidable calls to back-office staff, and a degraded field experience that compounds across every job.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## 3. Objectives
40	
41	| #   | Objective                                                | Measure                                                              |
42	| --- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
43	| O1  | Reduce time-to-find-asset on-site                        | Median lookup time < 10 seconds, any mode                            |
44	| O2  | Remove dependency on network connectivity for lookup     | 100% of pre-cached records resolvable offline, no crash/blank screen |
45	| O3  | Reduce back-office interruption calls for serial lookups | Qualitative: eliminated for pre-cached assets                        |
46	| O4  | Keep the solution operable without custom backend logic  | Zero Apex invocations at runtime (LDS/UI API/GraphQL only)           |
47	
48	---
49	
50	## 4. Scope
51	
52	### 4.1 In Scope
53	
54	- One LWC ("Asset Finder") with four entry modes: Recently Viewed (default), Text/typeahead search, Nearby (GPS) search, Barcode/QR scan.
55	- Navigation from any result to the standard Asset record detail page.
56	- Offline behavior via Salesforce Mobile Offline (Briefcase-cached data), scoped to the technician's assigned Accounts.
57	- Distance display in metric or imperial units, derived from the running user's locale.
58	- A radius selector (≥3 options) for nearby search, reactive without page reload.
59	- Graceful error/empty states for all four modes (no permission, no GPS, no camera, zero results, offline-with-no-cache).
60	- Desktop graceful degradation (component renders with no JS errors; barcode mode disabled/hidden where camera capability is absent).
61	- Placement as a new custom tab/Lightning app page in the mobile navigation, additive to the existing standard Assets tab.
62	
63	### 4.2 Out of Scope (this iteration)
64	
65	- Image-similarity or content-description search (mentioned in the broader problem framing around digital asset management generally, but not part of the three required modes below — flagged as a future consideration, see §14).
66	- Editing or creating Asset records from within the finder (read/navigate only).
67	- Cross-system asset consolidation (assets living outside Salesforce).
68	- A dedicated, purpose-built barcode field — this iteration matches scans against `SerialNumber` (see §9 Business Rules).
69	- Persisted (cross-session) user-level unit preference — this iteration derives units from locale each session.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## 5. Stakeholders & Personas
74	
75	| Role                                     | Interest                                                                           |
76	| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
77	| **Field Technician (primary persona)**   | Needs fast, reliable, offline-capable asset lookup on a mobile device.             |
78	| **Field Service / Operations Manager**   | Cares about technician productivity and reduced back-office load.                  |
79	| **Back-Office / Dispatch Support Staff** | Currently absorbs lookup calls; benefits from call volume reduction.               |
80	| **Salesforce Admin / Platform Team**     | Owns Briefcase/offline configuration, sharing model, and the mobile nav placement. |
81	| **Hackathon Solution/Dev Team**          | Builds and demos the component within the SDLC gates.                              |
82	
83	---
84	
85	## 6. Process — As-Is
86	
87	```mermaid
88	flowchart TD
89	    A[Technician arrives on-site] --> B{Knows exact asset name/ID?}
90	    B -- No --> C[Scroll long Asset list view]
91	    C --> D{Found it?}
92	    D -- No --> E[Call back-office to look up serial number]
93	    E --> F[Wait for response]
94	    F --> G[Return to list, search again]
95	    D -- Yes --> H[Open record]
96	    B -- Yes --> I[Type partial name into search]
97	    I --> J{Typo / mismatch?}
98	    J -- Yes --> C
99	    J -- No --> H
100	    G --> H
101	    H --> K[Perform field service work]
102	
103	    style E fill:#f66,color:#fff
104	    style C fill:#f90,color:#fff
105	```
106	
107	**Pain points highlighted:** unbounded list scrolling (C), office call dependency (E), and rework from mistyped search (J → back to C).
108	
109	### 6.1 Process — To-Be
110	
111	```mermaid
112	flowchart TD
113	    A[Technician opens Asset Finder] --> B[Recently Viewed shown by default]
114	    B --> C{Asset visible in recents?}
115	    C -- Yes --> Z[Tap result]
116	    C -- No --> D{Choose search mode}
117	    D -- Text --> E[Type name/identifier - typeahead results]
118	    D -- Nearby --> F[Grant/reuse GPS permission]
119	    F --> G[Select radius - reactive results ranked by distance]
120	    D -- Barcode --> H[Scan physical label]
121	    H --> I[Resolve SerialNumber to record]
122	    E --> Z
123	    G --> Z
124	    I --> Z
125	    Z --> J[Navigate to standard Asset record page]
126	    J --> K[Perform field service work]
127	
128	    B -.offline: served from Briefcase cache.-> B
129	    E -.offline: served from Briefcase cache.-> E
130	    G -.offline: served from Briefcase cache.-> G
131	    I -.offline: served from Briefcase cache.-> I
132	```
133	
134	**Key change:** every path converges on the record page in one to two taps, with no mode requiring network connectivity once the technician's Account-scoped Assets are cached.
135	
136	---
137	
138	## 7. Functional Requirements
139	
140	### 7.1 Recently Viewed (default view)
141	
142	| ID    | Requirement                                                                                        |
143	| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
144	| FR-01 | On component open, before any input, display the running user's recently viewed Asset records.     |
145	| FR-02 | Recently Viewed list must render from cached/offline-capable data (no Apex, no network-only call). |
146	| FR-03 | Selecting a Recently Viewed row navigates to that Asset's standard record page.                    |
147	| FR-04 | If no recently viewed records exist, display a meaningful empty state (not a blank screen).        |
148	
149	### 7.2 Text / Typeahead Search
150	
151	| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                              |
152	| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
153	| FR-05 | Technician can type a name or identifier; results populate as they type (typeahead).                                                     |
154	| FR-06 | Search must match against Asset `Name` at minimum; matching against `SerialNumber`/`ExternalIdentifier` is a stretch goal for this mode. |
155	| FR-07 | Search results are scoped to Assets visible to the running user under standard sharing (no elevated access).                             |
156	| FR-08 | Zero-match state shows a meaningful "no results" message, not an empty/blank list.                                                       |
157	| FR-09 | Selecting a search result navigates to that Asset's standard record page.                                                                |
158	
159	### 7.3 Nearby Search
160	
161	| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                                                       |
162	| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
163	| FR-10 | On selecting Nearby mode, the app requests the device's GPS coordinates via the browser Geolocation API.                                                          |
164	| FR-11 | Results are Assets with populated `Latitude`/`Longitude`, scoped to the technician's assigned Accounts (via Account Team membership), within the selected radius. |
165	| FR-12 | Results are ranked ascending by calculated distance from the technician's current position.                                                                       |
166	| FR-13 | Distance is displayed in metric (km) or imperial (mi) units, derived from the running user's locale.                                                              |
167	| FR-14 | A radius selector offers at least 3 discrete options; changing the radius updates results reactively, with no page reload.                                        |
168	| FR-15 | If GPS permission is denied or unavailable, display a meaningful message and do not crash the component.                                                          |
169	| FR-16 | If no Assets fall within the selected radius, display a meaningful empty state.                                                                                   |
170	| FR-17 | Selecting a nearby result navigates to that Asset's standard record page.                                                                                         |
171	
172	### 7.4 Barcode / QR Scan
173	
174	| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                              |
175	| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
176	| FR-18 | Technician can invoke the device camera to scan a barcode/QR label.                                                                      |
177	| FR-19 | The scanned value is matched against Asset `SerialNumber`.                                                                               |
178	| FR-20 | A successful match navigates directly to that Asset's standard record page — no intermediate result list.                                |
179	| FR-21 | If the scanned value matches no Asset, display a meaningful "not found" message.                                                         |
180	| FR-22 | If the device/browser has no camera or scanning capability (e.g., desktop), the barcode mode is disabled or hidden rather than erroring. |
181	
182	### 7.5 Cross-Cutting
183	
184	| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                 |
185	| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
186	| FR-23 | All four modes are accessible from one unified component (no separate pages to navigate between modes).                                                                                     |
187	| FR-24 | No raw error objects, stack traces, or technical error codes are ever shown to the technician — all failures map to a human-readable message.                                               |
188	| FR-25 | The component must render without JavaScript errors when opened in a desktop browser, degrading gracefully (e.g., barcode mode unavailable, GPS mode shows a permission prompt or message). |
189	| FR-26 | Record retrieval in all modes uses only the offline-capable data API (LDS / UI API / GraphQL wire adapters) — **no Apex controller is invoked at runtime**.                                 |
190	| FR-27 | Offline, all four modes operate against the pre-cached (Briefcase) dataset, returning cached results or a meaningful "not available offline" message — never a crash or blank screen.       |
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 8. Non-Functional Requirements
195	
196	| Category                 | Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
197	| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
198	| **Performance**          | Any search mode returns a usable result within the 10-second end-to-end target on a typical field network (or instantly offline).                                                                                              |
199	| **Availability/Offline** | Full functional parity for pre-cached records when the device has no network connectivity.                                                                                                                                     |
200	| **Security**             | No elevation of access — the component only surfaces Assets the running user already has read access to under org sharing rules (CRUD/FLS respected, no `without sharing` context, no Apex attack surface since none is used). |
201	| **Accessibility**        | Component usable via screen reader and keyboard navigation for all interactive elements (search input, radius selector, scan trigger, result rows).                                                                            |
202	| **Compatibility**        | Renders without error on both the Salesforce mobile app (primary) and desktop browser (secondary/demo).                                                                                                                        |
203	| **Localization**         | Distance units follow the running user's locale (metric/imperial) without additional configuration.                                                                                                                            |
204	| **Maintainability**      | Single component, no custom Apex/backend to maintain; relies on standard Lightning Data Service / UI API / GraphQL wire adapters.                                                                                              |
205	
206	---
207	
208	## 9. Data Model — Grounded Against Target Org (`hack28`)
209	
210	No new custom object is required. The standard **Asset** object already carries every field this use case needs (verified via org describe):
211	
212	| Business Need         | Asset Field                            | Type      | Notes                                                                                             |
213	| --------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
214	| Display name          | `Name`                                 | string    | Primary label in all result lists                                                                 |
215	| Barcode/QR match      | `SerialNumber`                         | string    | Matched against scanned value (FR-19)                                                             |
216	| Nearby ranking        | `Latitude` / `Longitude`               | double    | Top-level fields, not nested under the `Address` compound field                                   |
217	| Status context        | `Status`, `StatusReason`               | picklist  | Available for future filtering (e.g., exclude retired assets)                                     |
218	| Sharing/scope         | `AccountId`, `OwnerId`                 | reference | Drives Account-based offline scoping (§9.1)                                                       |
219	| Site reference        | `LocationId`                           | reference | Available for future site-level grouping                                                          |
220	| Fallback external key | `ExternalIdentifier`, `External_ID__c` | string    | Not used in this iteration; documented as a future fallback if `SerialNumber` proves insufficient |
221	
222	**Supporting object (offline scoping dependency):** `AccountTeamMember` (`AccountId`, `UserId`) — verified present in the target org — is the mechanism by which a technician's Account assignments are determined for Briefcase scoping.
223	
224	**Data readiness gap (flagged, not blocking):** `Latitude`/`Longitude` population on existing Asset records is not verified and should be confirmed as a discovery/UAT data-seeding task before nearby search can be demoed meaningfully.
225	
226	---
227	
228	## 10. Business Rules
229	
230	| #     | Rule                                                                                                                                                                           |
231	| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
232	| BR-01 | An Asset is eligible for offline pre-caching for a technician only if it is linked (via `AccountId`) to an Account where the technician is listed as an `AccountTeamMember`.   |
233	| BR-02 | A barcode/QR scan resolves against `Asset.SerialNumber` only; a scan with no matching `SerialNumber` is treated as "not found," not an error.                                  |
234	| BR-03 | Distance units (km vs. mi) are derived from the running user's Salesforce locale at render time; no manual toggle is persisted in this iteration.                              |
235	| BR-04 | The nearby radius selector must offer a minimum of 3 options; default radius and exact values are proposed in Epics/Story detail and confirmed with stakeholders before build. |
236	| BR-05 | Selecting any result, from any mode, always navigates to the standard Asset record page — there is no mode-specific detail view.                                               |
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 11. Assumptions
241	
242	- A1: The technician persona has at least one Account assignment via Account Team membership; technicians with zero assigned Accounts will see an empty Recently Viewed/Nearby state by design (not a defect).
243	- A2: The Salesforce Mobile App (not a third-party wrapper) is the deployment target, so `lightning/mobileCapabilities` and Mobile Offline/Briefcase are available.
244	- A3: Physical asset labels are printed with a barcode/QR encoding the exact `SerialNumber` value stored on the Asset record.
245	- A4: The org's existing sharing model on Asset is fit for purpose — this component does not change sharing, only reads within it.
246	- A5: Demo/UAT environments will have Lat/Long-populated Asset records seeded ahead of testing nearby search.
247	
248	## 12. Constraints
249	
250	- C1: No Apex may be invoked at runtime (hard constraint from the problem statement's success criteria).
251	- C2: Distance calculation has no native "distance from point" operator in UI API/GraphQL — must be computed client-side in JavaScript (Haversine formula) after a bounded server-side fetch.
252	- C3: Offline caching is bounded by Salesforce Mobile Offline/Briefcase configuration limits — the Account-based scoping (BR-01) exists specifically to keep the cached payload within those limits.
253	
254	## 13. Dependencies
255	
256	- D1: Briefcase Builder configuration (admin-side) for the Account-scoped Asset rule — a platform configuration task, not a code deliverable, but required before offline testing.
257	- D2: Demo data — Accounts, AccountTeamMember assignments, and Lat/Long-populated Assets — must exist in the target org before UAT.
258	- D3: Device/browser support for `navigator.geolocation` and `lightning/mobileCapabilities` barcode scanning (native mobile app; degraded on desktop per FR-25/FR-22).
259	
260	---
261	
262	## 14. Risks & Mitigations
263	
264	| #   | Risk                                                                                 | Impact                                                                               | Mitigation                                                                                                                                                           |
265	| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
266	| R1  | Lat/Long fields empty on real Asset data                                             | Nearby search returns nothing, looks broken in demo                                  | Seed/validate demo data early in discovery; add explicit "location not available" state distinct from "no assets in range"                                           |
267	| R2  | Client-side distance calc over a large Account-scoped result set impacts performance | Miss the <10s target                                                                 | Bound the initial GraphQL fetch with a coarse Lat/Long range filter before client-side Haversine sort, rather than pulling the full Account-scoped set               |
268	| R3  | Barcode labels don't encode `SerialNumber` in the field's actual print format        | Scans never resolve (BR-02 assumption false)                                         | Confirm label format with stakeholders during Epics/Story refinement; `ExternalIdentifier`/`External_ID__c` documented as a fallback field if this assumption breaks |
269	| R4  | Desktop demo environment has no camera/GPS                                           | Barcode/Nearby modes look "broken" to reviewers unfamiliar with graceful degradation | Explicit degraded-state UI copy so the behavior reads as intentional, not a bug                                                                                      |
270	| R5  | Offline Briefcase rule misconfigured or absent at demo time                          | "Offline" success criteria cannot be shown                                           | Track Briefcase setup as an explicit dependency (D1) with its own checklist item, not assumed complete because the LWC is done                                       |
271	
272	---
273	
274	## 15. Success Criteria Traceability
275	
276	| Original Success Criterion (PS-02)                               | Covered By                               |
277	| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
278	| Locate via text search, proximity, or barcode scan               | FR-05–FR-09, FR-10–FR-17, FR-18–FR-22    |
279	| Offline mode returns cached results, no crash/blank screen       | FR-27, §9.1 Briefcase scoping, BR-01     |
280	| Nearby results display distance in user's unit (metric/imperial) | FR-13, BR-03                             |
281	| Radius selector ≥3 options, reactive                             | FR-14, BR-04                             |
282	| Any result navigates to standard record page                     | FR-03, FR-09, FR-17, FR-20, BR-05        |
283	| Meaningful error/empty states, no raw errors shown               | FR-04, FR-08, FR-15, FR-16, FR-21, FR-24 |
284	| Renders without JS errors in desktop browser                     | FR-22, FR-25                             |
285	| No Apex at runtime                                               | FR-26, C1                                |
286	
287	---
288	
289	## 16. Out of Scope / Future Considerations
290	
291	- Image-similarity / free-text content-description search across stored digital assets (broader Digital Asset Management framing in the business context, not required by the three specified modes).
292	- Persisted, user-configurable unit preference (currently locale-derived only).
293	- Matching barcode scans against fields other than `SerialNumber`.
294	- Editing/creating Assets from the finder.
295	- Cross-system asset search beyond Salesforce.
296	
297	---
298	
299	## 17. Glossary
300	
301	| Term          | Definition                                                                                                     |
302	| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
303	| **LDS**       | Lightning Data Service — the client-side data layer used by UI API/GraphQL wire adapters, offline-cache-aware. |
304	| **Briefcase** | Salesforce Mobile Offline's rule-based mechanism for pre-caching a bounded record set to a device.             |
305	| **Typeahead** | Search results that populate incrementally as the user types, without an explicit submit action.               |
306	| **MRU**       | Most Recently Used — the basis for the "Recently Viewed" list.                                                 |
307

**Business impact:** lost technician productivity per site visit, avoidable calls to back-office staff, and a degraded field experience that compounds across every job.

---

## 3. Objectives

| #   | Objective                                                | Measure                                                              |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| O1  | Reduce time-to-find-asset on-site                        | Median lookup time < 10 seconds, any mode                            |
| O2  | Remove dependency on network connectivity for lookup     | 100% of pre-cached records resolvable offline, no crash/blank screen |
| O3  | Reduce back-office interruption calls for serial lookups | Qualitative: eliminated for pre-cached assets                        |
| O4  | Keep the solution operable without custom backend logic  | Zero Apex invocations at runtime (LDS/UI API/GraphQL only)           |

---

## 4. Scope

### 4.1 In Scope

- One LWC ("Asset Finder") with four entry modes: Recently Viewed (default), Text/typeahead search, Nearby (GPS) search, Barcode/QR scan.
- Navigation from any result to the standard Asset record detail page.
- Offline behavior via Salesforce Mobile Offline (Briefcase-cached data), scoped to the technician's assigned Accounts.
- Distance display in metric or imperial units, derived from the running user's locale.
- A radius selector (≥3 options) for nearby search, reactive without page reload.
- Graceful error/empty states for all four modes (no permission, no GPS, no camera, zero results, offline-with-no-cache).
- Desktop graceful degradation (component renders with no JS errors; barcode mode disabled/hidden where camera capability is absent).
- Placement as a new custom tab/Lightning app page in the mobile navigation, additive to the existing standard Assets tab.

### 4.2 Out of Scope (this iteration)

- Image-similarity or content-description search (mentioned in the broader problem framing around digital asset management generally, but not part of the three required modes below — flagged as a future consideration, see §14).
- Editing or creating Asset records from within the finder (read/navigate only).
- Cross-system asset consolidation (assets living outside Salesforce).
- A dedicated, purpose-built barcode field — this iteration matches scans against `SerialNumber` (see §9 Business Rules).
- Persisted (cross-session) user-level unit preference — this iteration derives units from locale each session.

---

## 5. Stakeholders & Personas

| Role                                     | Interest                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Field Technician (primary persona)**   | Needs fast, reliable, offline-capable asset lookup on a mobile device.             |
| **Field Service / Operations Manager**   | Cares about technician productivity and reduced back-office load.                  |
| **Back-Office / Dispatch Support Staff** | Currently absorbs lookup calls; benefits from call volume reduction.               |
| **Salesforce Admin / Platform Team**     | Owns Briefcase/offline configuration, sharing model, and the mobile nav placement. |
| **Hackathon Solution/Dev Team**          | Builds and demos the component within the SDLC gates.                              |

---

## 6. Process — As-Is

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Technician arrives on-site] --> B{Knows exact asset name/ID?}
    B -- No --> C[Scroll long Asset list view]
    C --> D{Found it?}
    D -- No --> E[Call back-office to look up serial number]
    E --> F[Wait for response]
    F --> G[Return to list, search again]
    D -- Yes --> H[Open record]
    B -- Yes --> I[Type partial name into search]
    I --> J{Typo / mismatch?}
    J -- Yes --> C
    J -- No --> H
    G --> H
    H --> K[Perform field service work]

    style E fill:#f66,color:#fff
    style C fill:#f90,color:#fff
```

**Pain points highlighted:** unbounded list scrolling (C), office call dependency (E), and rework from mistyped search (J → back to C).

### 6.1 Process — To-Be

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Technician opens Asset Finder] --> B[Recently Viewed shown by default]
    B --> C{Asset visible in recents?}
    C -- Yes --> Z[Tap result]
    C -- No --> D{Choose search mode}
    D -- Text --> E[Type name/identifier - typeahead results]
    D -- Nearby --> F[Grant/reuse GPS permission]
    F --> G[Select radius - reactive results ranked by distance]
    D -- Barcode --> H[Scan physical label]
    H --> I[Resolve SerialNumber to record]
    E --> Z
    G --> Z
    I --> Z
    Z --> J[Navigate to standard Asset record page]
    J --> K[Perform field service work]

    B -.offline: served from Briefcase cache.-> B
    E -.offline: served from Briefcase cache.-> E
    G -.offline: served from Briefcase cache.-> G
    I -.offline: served from Briefcase cache.-> I
```

**Key change:** every path converges on the record page in one to two taps, with no mode requiring network connectivity once the technician's Account-scoped Assets are cached.

---

## 7. Functional Requirements

### 7.1 Recently Viewed (default view)

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                        |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| FR-01 | On component open, before any input, display the running user's recently viewed Asset records.     |
| FR-02 | Recently Viewed list must render from cached/offline-capable data (no Apex, no network-only call). |
| FR-03 | Selecting a Recently Viewed row navigates to that Asset's standard record page.                    |
| FR-04 | If no recently viewed records exist, display a meaningful empty state (not a blank screen).        |

### 7.2 Text / Typeahead Search

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                              |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| FR-05 | Technician can type a name or identifier; results populate as they type (typeahead).                                                     |
| FR-06 | Search must match against Asset `Name` at minimum; matching against `SerialNumber`/`ExternalIdentifier` is a stretch goal for this mode. |
| FR-07 | Search results are scoped to Assets visible to the running user under standard sharing (no elevated access).                             |
| FR-08 | Zero-match state shows a meaningful "no results" message, not an empty/blank list.                                                       |
| FR-09 | Selecting a search result navigates to that Asset's standard record page.                                                                |

### 7.3 Nearby Search

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| FR-10 | On selecting Nearby mode, the app requests the device's GPS coordinates via the browser Geolocation API.                                                          |
| FR-11 | Results are Assets with populated `Latitude`/`Longitude`, scoped to the technician's assigned Accounts (via Account Team membership), within the selected radius. |
| FR-12 | Results are ranked ascending by calculated distance from the technician's current position.                                                                       |
| FR-13 | Distance is displayed in metric (km) or imperial (mi) units, derived from the running user's locale.                                                              |
| FR-14 | A radius selector offers at least 3 discrete options; changing the radius updates results reactively, with no page reload.                                        |
| FR-15 | If GPS permission is denied or unavailable, display a meaningful message and do not crash the component.                                                          |
| FR-16 | If no Assets fall within the selected radius, display a meaningful empty state.                                                                                   |
| FR-17 | Selecting a nearby result navigates to that Asset's standard record page.                                                                                         |

### 7.4 Barcode / QR Scan

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                              |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| FR-18 | Technician can invoke the device camera to scan a barcode/QR label.                                                                      |
| FR-19 | The scanned value is matched against Asset `SerialNumber`.                                                                               |
| FR-20 | A successful match navigates directly to that Asset's standard record page — no intermediate result list.                                |
| FR-21 | If the scanned value matches no Asset, display a meaningful "not found" message.                                                         |
| FR-22 | If the device/browser has no camera or scanning capability (e.g., desktop), the barcode mode is disabled or hidden rather than erroring. |

### 7.5 Cross-Cutting

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| FR-23 | All four modes are accessible from one unified component (no separate pages to navigate between modes).                                                                                     |
| FR-24 | No raw error objects, stack traces, or technical error codes are ever shown to the technician — all failures map to a human-readable message.                                               |
| FR-25 | The component must render without JavaScript errors when opened in a desktop browser, degrading gracefully (e.g., barcode mode unavailable, GPS mode shows a permission prompt or message). |
| FR-26 | Record retrieval in all modes uses only the offline-capable data API (LDS / UI API / GraphQL wire adapters) — **no Apex controller is invoked at runtime**.                                 |
| FR-27 | Offline, all four modes operate against the pre-cached (Briefcase) dataset, returning cached results or a meaningful "not available offline" message — never a crash or blank screen.       |

---

## 8. Non-Functional Requirements

| Category                 | Requirement                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Performance**          | Any search mode returns a usable result within the 10-second end-to-end target on a typical field network (or instantly offline).                                                                                              |
| **Availability/Offline** | Full functional parity for pre-cached records when the device has no network connectivity.                                                                                                                                     |
| **Security**             | No elevation of access — the component only surfaces Assets the running user already has read access to under org sharing rules (CRUD/FLS respected, no `without sharing` context, no Apex attack surface since none is used). |
| **Accessibility**        | Component usable via screen reader and keyboard navigation for all interactive elements (search input, radius selector, scan trigger, result rows).                                                                            |
| **Compatibility**        | Renders without error on both the Salesforce mobile app (primary) and desktop browser (secondary/demo).                                                                                                                        |
| **Localization**         | Distance units follow the running user's locale (metric/imperial) without additional configuration.                                                                                                                            |
| **Maintainability**      | Single component, no custom Apex/backend to maintain; relies on standard Lightning Data Service / UI API / GraphQL wire adapters.                                                                                              |

---

## 9. Data Model — Grounded Against Target Org (`hack28`)

No new custom object is required. The standard **Asset** object already carries every field this use case needs (verified via org describe):

| Business Need         | Asset Field                            | Type      | Notes                                                                                             |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Display name          | `Name`                                 | string    | Primary label in all result lists                                                                 |
| Barcode/QR match      | `SerialNumber`                         | string    | Matched against scanned value (FR-19)                                                             |
| Nearby ranking        | `Latitude` / `Longitude`               | double    | Top-level fields, not nested under the `Address` compound field                                   |
| Status context        | `Status`, `StatusReason`               | picklist  | Available for future filtering (e.g., exclude retired assets)                                     |
| Sharing/scope         | `AccountId`, `OwnerId`                 | reference | Drives Account-based offline scoping (§9.1)                                                       |
| Site reference        | `LocationId`                           | reference | Available for future site-level grouping                                                          |
| Fallback external key | `ExternalIdentifier`, `External_ID__c` | string    | Not used in this iteration; documented as a future fallback if `SerialNumber` proves insufficient |

**Supporting object (offline scoping dependency):** `AccountTeamMember` (`AccountId`, `UserId`) — verified present in the target org — is the mechanism by which a technician's Account assignments are determined for Briefcase scoping.

**Data readiness gap (flagged, not blocking):** `Latitude`/`Longitude` population on existing Asset records is not verified and should be confirmed as a discovery/UAT data-seeding task before nearby search can be demoed meaningfully.

---

## 10. Business Rules

| #     | Rule                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| BR-01 | An Asset is eligible for offline pre-caching for a technician only if it is linked (via `AccountId`) to an Account where the technician is listed as an `AccountTeamMember`.   |
| BR-02 | A barcode/QR scan resolves against `Asset.SerialNumber` only; a scan with no matching `SerialNumber` is treated as "not found," not an error.                                  |
| BR-03 | Distance units (km vs. mi) are derived from the running user's Salesforce locale at render time; no manual toggle is persisted in this iteration.                              |
| BR-04 | The nearby radius selector must offer a minimum of 3 options; default radius and exact values are proposed in Epics/Story detail and confirmed with stakeholders before build. |
| BR-05 | Selecting any result, from any mode, always navigates to the standard Asset record page — there is no mode-specific detail view.                                               |

---

## 11. Assumptions

- A1: The technician persona has at least one Account assignment via Account Team membership; technicians with zero assigned Accounts will see an empty Recently Viewed/Nearby state by design (not a defect).
- A2: The Salesforce Mobile App (not a third-party wrapper) is the deployment target, so `lightning/mobileCapabilities` and Mobile Offline/Briefcase are available.
- A3: Physical asset labels are printed with a barcode/QR encoding the exact `SerialNumber` value stored on the Asset record.
- A4: The org's existing sharing model on Asset is fit for purpose — this component does not change sharing, only reads within it.
- A5: Demo/UAT environments will have Lat/Long-populated Asset records seeded ahead of testing nearby search.

## 12. Constraints

- C1: No Apex may be invoked at runtime (hard constraint from the problem statement's success criteria).
- C2: Distance calculation has no native "distance from point" operator in UI API/GraphQL — must be computed client-side in JavaScript (Haversine formula) after a bounded server-side fetch.
- C3: Offline caching is bounded by Salesforce Mobile Offline/Briefcase configuration limits — the Account-based scoping (BR-01) exists specifically to keep the cached payload within those limits.

## 13. Dependencies

- D1: Briefcase Builder configuration (admin-side) for the Account-scoped Asset rule — a platform configuration task, not a code deliverable, but required before offline testing.
- D2: Demo data — Accounts, AccountTeamMember assignments, and Lat/Long-populated Assets — must exist in the target org before UAT.
- D3: Device/browser support for `navigator.geolocation` and `lightning/mobileCapabilities` barcode scanning (native mobile app; degraded on desktop per FR-25/FR-22).

---

## 14. Risks & Mitigations

| #   | Risk                                                                                 | Impact                                                                               | Mitigation                                                                                                                                                           |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| R1  | Lat/Long fields empty on real Asset data                                             | Nearby search returns nothing, looks broken in demo                                  | Seed/validate demo data early in discovery; add explicit "location not available" state distinct from "no assets in range"                                           |
| R2  | Client-side distance calc over a large Account-scoped result set impacts performance | Miss the <10s target                                                                 | Bound the initial GraphQL fetch with a coarse Lat/Long range filter before client-side Haversine sort, rather than pulling the full Account-scoped set               |
| R3  | Barcode labels don't encode `SerialNumber` in the field's actual print format        | Scans never resolve (BR-02 assumption false)                                         | Confirm label format with stakeholders during Epics/Story refinement; `ExternalIdentifier`/`External_ID__c` documented as a fallback field if this assumption breaks |
| R4  | Desktop demo environment has no camera/GPS                                           | Barcode/Nearby modes look "broken" to reviewers unfamiliar with graceful degradation | Explicit degraded-state UI copy so the behavior reads as intentional, not a bug                                                                                      |
| R5  | Offline Briefcase rule misconfigured or absent at demo time                          | "Offline" success criteria cannot be shown                                           | Track Briefcase setup as an explicit dependency (D1) with its own checklist item, not assumed complete because the LWC is done                                       |

---

## 15. Success Criteria Traceability

| Original Success Criterion (PS-02)                               | Covered By                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Locate via text search, proximity, or barcode scan               | FR-05–FR-09, FR-10–FR-17, FR-18–FR-22    |
| Offline mode returns cached results, no crash/blank screen       | FR-27, §9.1 Briefcase scoping, BR-01     |
| Nearby results display distance in user's unit (metric/imperial) | FR-13, BR-03                             |
| Radius selector ≥3 options, reactive                             | FR-14, BR-04                             |
| Any result navigates to standard record page                     | FR-03, FR-09, FR-17, FR-20, BR-05        |
| Meaningful error/empty states, no raw errors shown               | FR-04, FR-08, FR-15, FR-16, FR-21, FR-24 |
| Renders without JS errors in desktop browser                     | FR-22, FR-25                             |
| No Apex at runtime                                               | FR-26, C1                                |

---

## 16. Out of Scope / Future Considerations

- Image-similarity / free-text content-description search across stored digital assets (broader Digital Asset Management framing in the business context, not required by the three specified modes).
- Persisted, user-configurable unit preference (currently locale-derived only).
- Matching barcode scans against fields other than `SerialNumber`.
- Editing/creating Assets from the finder.
- Cross-system asset search beyond Salesforce.

---

## 17. Glossary

| Term          | Definition                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **LDS**       | Lightning Data Service — the client-side data layer used by UI API/GraphQL wire adapters, offline-cache-aware. |
| **Briefcase** | Salesforce Mobile Offline's rule-based mechanism for pre-caching a bounded record set to a device.             |
| **Typeahead** | Search results that populate incrementally as the user types, without an explicit submit action.               |
| **MRU**       | Most Recently Used — the basis for the "Recently Viewed" list.                                                 |

20	
21	# Architecture Spine — Multi-Modal Asset Finder
22	
23	A single Salesforce Lightning Web Component that replaces the default equipment list view and finds an equipment record in under 10 seconds by text, proximity, barcode/QR, recents, or image/description — trustworthy offline and in degraded conditions. This spine fixes the invariants the seven epics' stories must share; the code owns everything below.
24	
25	## Design Paradigm
26	
27	**Ports & Adapters (Hexagonal), inside one LWC.** Each find mode is an **adapter** behind a single `ResultProvider` **port**; a core **orchestrator** depends only on the port, never on a mode's specifics. Platform access (data, scanner, GPS, navigation) sits behind thin **infrastructure adapters** so the core stays free of Salesforce API detail and every mode composes the same way. This is what lets FR14 be an isolated online provider, offline be a data-layer concern, and desktop degradation be a capability lookup — without touching core.
28	
29	Layer → directory map:
30	
31	```text
32	force-app/main/default/lwc/
33	  assetFinder/            # ORCHESTRATOR (core): owns state, dispatch, StateView routing
34	  finderModes/            # ADAPTERS: text, nearby, scan, recents, snapDescribe (presentational)
35	  finderResult/           # shared result card + disambiguation list (presentational)
36	  finderStateView/        # single degraded/empty/error/offline renderer
37	  finderShared/           # PORTS + domain: ResultProvider, EquipmentResult, StateResult, AppError
38	  service/                # INFRA ADAPTERS: graphqlData, capability, geolocation, navigation
39	```
40	
41	## Invariants & Rules
42	
43	Dependency direction (arrows = "may depend on"; nothing points back):
44	
45	```mermaid
46	graph TD
47	  UI[Mode adapters + result/state views] --> ORCH[assetFinder orchestrator]
48	  ORCH --> PORT[ResultProvider port + domain types]
49	  PROV[Provider implementations] --> PORT
50	  PROV --> INFRA[Infra adapters: graphqlData / capability / geolocation / navigation]
51	  INFRA --> PORT
52	  ORCH -. never .-> PROV
53	  UI -. never .-> INFRA
54	```
55	
56	### AD-1 — Ports & Adapters paradigm
57	
58	- **Binds:** all
59	- **Prevents:** mode-specific logic leaking into the core; incompatible per-mode integrations.
60	- **Rule:** The orchestrator depends only on the `ResultProvider` port and domain types. Mode logic lives in adapters; Salesforce platform calls live only in infra adapters.
61	
62	### AD-2 — Single `ResultProvider` port
63	
64	- **Binds:** CAP-1, CAP-2, CAP-3, CAP-4, CAP-5, FR14
65	- **Prevents:** N bespoke mode integrations; two owners of the query flow.
66	- **Rule:** Every mode implements `search(criteria): Promise<EquipmentResult[]>` (throwing typed `AppError`). The orchestrator invokes modes only through this signature.
67	
68	### AD-3 — Normalized `EquipmentResult` is the only shape crossing the port
69	
70	- **Binds:** all modes, `finderResult`
71	- **Prevents:** divergent per-mode result shapes breaking the shared list + disambiguation.
72	- **Rule:** The sole result DTO is `{ recordId, name, distinguishingFields: string[], distanceMeters?, source, confidence? }`. Distance is carried in **meters**; unit formatting happens only at the view edge (FR10). `confidence` is `0..1` where present, else `undefined`.
73	  - **`distinguishingFields` contract:** pre-formatted, human-readable labels only — never raw codes mixed with labels. Per mode: text/scan → `[identifier]` (+ `barcodeValue` only when it disambiguates); nearby → `[identifier, distanceLabel]`; recents → `[identifier, lastViewedLabel]`; snapDescribe → `[identifier, confidenceLabel]`. Length is stable within a mode and never zero.
74	  - **Result ordering:** each provider returns results already ranked best-first by its own relevance key (text = match strength; nearby = ascending `distanceMeters`; recents = most-recent-first; snapDescribe = descending `confidence`). The orchestrator preserves provider order and never re-sorts across modes.
75	
76	### AD-4 — One GraphQL/LDS data layer, no runtime Apex `[ADOPTED]`
77	
78	- **Binds:** all data retrieval (CAP-1..6)
79	- **Prevents:** Apex creep, uncached offline reads, scattered data access.
80	- **Rule:** Records are read only through the `graphqlData` service using the `lightning/uiGraphQLApi` wire over LDS/Briefcase. No `@salesforce/apex` at runtime. Offline correctness is this layer's responsibility.
81	
82	### AD-5 — Capability detection is a boundary, owned by the orchestrator
83	
84	- **Binds:** scan, nearby, snapDescribe, desktop degradation (NFR3, NFR6)
85	- **Prevents:** desktop crashes, duplicated detection, feature-detection false positives, mode/orchestrator disagreement on availability.
86	- **Rule:** A single `capability` service feature-detects scanner/GPS/camera/network **and verifies at invocation**. Nothing else calls `getBarcodeScanner`, `navigator.geolocation`, or UA-sniffs. The **orchestrator** (never a mode) queries the service and passes an `availableModes: string[]` prop down; the mode selector renders unavailable modes as disabled with a tip. A mode never self-detects or self-disables. If a capability drops mid-flight, the mode throws `AppError` and the orchestrator re-derives availability.
87	
88	### AD-6 — Dispatch-token concurrency invariant; orchestrator owns the clock
89	
90	- **Binds:** orchestrator, all async modes (M2, M4, NFR3)
91	- **Prevents:** out-of-order or wrong-mode results rendering as current; split timeout ownership.
92	- **Rule:** Every async request carries a token = `{ mode, query, unit: 'm'|'ft'|'km', radius?: number, seq }`, where `mode ∈ {text, nearby, scan, recents, snapDescribe}`. Any response whose token ≠ current state is discarded, never rendered; mode switches and new input supersede in-flight requests. Changing `unit` alone does not re-dispatch text/scan/recents (they ignore it); it re-dispatches only nearby (distance labels change). The **orchestrator alone** enforces the per-mode deadline (AD-7) and is the only source of a `timeout` state — modes never start their own timeout timer nor throw `timeout`.
93	
94	### AD-7 — Definite-state invariant; empty ≠ error
95	
96	- **Binds:** all modes, `finderStateView` (NFR2, M3)
97	- **Prevents:** indefinite spinners, blank screens, and "found nothing" being confused with "couldn't run".
98	- **Rule:** Every search resolves to exactly one `StateResult` ∈ `{ results, empty, timeout, error, offline }` within its budget (core 10s; FR14 15s). Timeouts and errors always offer Retry or a fallback. **A provider signals zero matches by returning `[]` (→ `empty`), never by throwing** — a thrown `AppError` always means the search could not complete. The orchestrator maps `[]`→`empty`, deadline expiry→`timeout`, and `AppError` by kind (AD-11).
99	
100	### AD-8 — Navigation to standard record page only `[ADOPTED]`
101	
102	- **Binds:** CAP-6
103	- **Prevents:** reinventing record detail; two owners of the detail surface.
104	- **Rule:** Result selection navigates via `NavigationMixin` to the standard equipment record page. The component owns **find**, never **detail**.
105	
106	### AD-9 — FR14 is an isolated, online-only, pluggable provider
107	
108	- **Binds:** FR14
109	- **Prevents:** vision-service coupling into the offline/core path; high swap cost.
110	- **Rule:** Snap/Describe implements `ResultProvider` like any mode but is **online-only** (feature-detected off when offline), carries its own 15s budget, and returns `confidence`-scored results. No core or offline path may depend on it. The concrete vision service sits behind the provider and is replaceable without touching core.
111	
112	### AD-10 — Unidirectional state ownership
113	
114	- **Binds:** orchestrator, all subcomponents
115	- **Prevents:** two owners of component state.
116	- **Rule:** Providers and infra adapters are read-only (return data / throw `AppError`). The `assetFinder` orchestrator owns all reactive state. Mode/result subcomponents are presentational: props down, events up. No child mutates shared state or calls a provider directly.
117	
118	### AD-11 — Single degraded-state renderer, disjoint typed errors
119	
120	- **Binds:** all modes (FR8, NFR7)
121	- **Prevents:** inconsistent or raw error UI; PII/existence leaks; overlapping error kinds.
122	- **Rule:** Providers throw typed `AppError { kind, userMessage, cause? }`; only `userMessage` reaches the DOM; the orchestrator maps `kind` to a `StateResult`; `finderStateView` renders every degraded state. The kinds are **disjoint** (no scenario maps to two): `offline` = network unavailable; `not-cached` = offline and the record isn't in the LDS cache; `no-access` = platform denied record/field visibility (record-level or FLS); `capability` = the required device capability is off/denied (scanner/GPS/camera); `api` = any other service/parse fault. There is **no `no-match` kind** (zero matches is `[]`, AD-7) and **no separate `permission` kind** (device permission → `capability`, data permission → `no-access`). `no-access`/`not-cached` never leak record existence or fields.
123	
124	### AD-12 — Access control is the platform's job; the component never re-implements it
