# Architecture Spine — Multi-Modal Asset Finder

A single Salesforce Lightning Web Component that replaces the default equipment list view and finds an equipment record in under 10 seconds by text, proximity, barcode/QR, recents, or image/description — trustworthy offline and in degraded conditions. This spine fixes the invariants the seven epics' stories must share; the code owns everything below.

## Design Paradigm

**Ports & Adapters (Hexagonal), inside one LWC.** Each find mode is an **adapter** behind a single `ResultProvider` **port**; a core **orchestrator** depends only on the port, never on a mode's specifics. Platform access (data, scanner, GPS, navigation) sits behind thin **infrastructure adapters** so the core stays free of Salesforce API detail and every mode composes the same way. This is what lets FR14 be an isolated online provider, offline be a data-layer concern, and desktop degradation be a capability lookup — without touching core.

Layer → directory map:

```text
force-app/main/default/lwc/
  assetFinder/            # ORCHESTRATOR (core): owns state, dispatch, StateView routing
  finderModes/            # ADAPTERS: text, nearby, scan, recents, snapDescribe (presentational)
  finderResult/           # shared result card + disambiguation list (presentational)
  finderStateView/        # single degraded/empty/error/offline renderer
  finderShared/           # PORTS + domain: ResultProvider, EquipmentResult, StateResult, AppError
  service/                # INFRA ADAPTERS: graphqlData, capability, geolocation, navigation
```

## Invariants & Rules

Dependency direction (arrows = "may depend on"; nothing points back):

```mermaid
graph TD
  UI[Mode adapters + result/state views] --> ORCH[assetFinder orchestrator]
  ORCH --> PORT[ResultProvider port + domain types]
  PROV[Provider implementations] --> PORT
  PROV --> INFRA[Infra adapters: graphqlData / capability / geolocation / navigation]
  INFRA --> PORT
  ORCH -. never .-> PROV
  UI -. never .-> INFRA
```

### AD-1 — Ports & Adapters paradigm

- **Binds:** all
- **Prevents:** mode-specific logic leaking into the core; incompatible per-mode integrations.
- **Rule:** The orchestrator depends only on the `ResultProvider` port and domain types. Mode logic lives in adapters; Salesforce platform calls live only in infra adapters.

### AD-2 — Single `ResultProvider` port

- **Binds:** CAP-1, CAP-2, CAP-3, CAP-4, CAP-5, FR14
- **Prevents:** N bespoke mode integrations; two owners of the query flow.
- **Rule:** Every mode implements `search(criteria): Promise<EquipmentResult[]>` (throwing typed `AppError`). The orchestrator invokes modes only through this signature.

### AD-3 — Normalized `EquipmentResult` is the only shape crossing the port

- **Binds:** all modes, `finderResult`
- **Prevents:** divergent per-mode result shapes breaking the shared list + disambiguation.
- **Rule:** The sole result DTO is `{ recordId, name, distinguishingFields: string[], distanceMeters?, source, confidence? }`. Distance is carried in **meters**; unit formatting happens only at the view edge (FR10). `confidence` is `0..1` where present, else `undefined`.
  - **`distinguishingFields` contract:** pre-formatted, human-readable labels only — never raw codes mixed with labels. Per mode: text/scan → `[identifier]` (+ `barcodeValue` only when it disambiguates); nearby → `[identifier, distanceLabel]`; recents → `[identifier, lastViewedLabel]`; snapDescribe → `[identifier, confidenceLabel]`. Length is stable within a mode and never zero.
  - **Result ordering:** each provider returns results already ranked best-first by its own relevance key (text = match strength; nearby = ascending `distanceMeters`; recents = most-recent-first; snapDescribe = descending `confidence`). The orchestrator preserves provider order and never re-sorts across modes.

### AD-4 — One GraphQL/LDS data layer, no runtime Apex `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** all data retrieval (CAP-1..6)
- **Prevents:** Apex creep, uncached offline reads, scattered data access.
- **Rule:** Records are read only through the `graphqlData` service using the `lightning/uiGraphQLApi` wire over LDS/Briefcase. No `@salesforce/apex` at runtime. Offline correctness is this layer's responsibility.

### AD-5 — Capability detection is a boundary, owned by the orchestrator

- **Binds:** scan, nearby, snapDescribe, desktop degradation (NFR3, NFR6)
- **Prevents:** desktop crashes, duplicated detection, feature-detection false positives, mode/orchestrator disagreement on availability.
- **Rule:** A single `capability` service feature-detects scanner/GPS/camera/network **and verifies at invocation**. Nothing else calls `getBarcodeScanner`, `navigator.geolocation`, or UA-sniffs. The **orchestrator** (never a mode) queries the service and passes an `availableModes: string[]` prop down; the mode selector renders unavailable modes as disabled with a tip. A mode never self-detects or self-disables. If a capability drops mid-flight, the mode throws `AppError` and the orchestrator re-derives availability.

### AD-6 — Dispatch-token concurrency invariant; orchestrator owns the clock

- **Binds:** orchestrator, all async modes (M2, M4, NFR3)
- **Prevents:** out-of-order or wrong-mode results rendering as current; split timeout ownership.
- **Rule:** Every async request carries a token = `{ mode, query, unit: 'm'|'ft'|'km', radius?: number, seq }`, where `mode ∈ {text, nearby, scan, recents, snapDescribe}`. Any response whose token ≠ current state is discarded, never rendered; mode switches and new input supersede in-flight requests. Changing `unit` alone does not re-dispatch text/scan/recents (they ignore it); it re-dispatches only nearby (distance labels change). The **orchestrator alone** enforces the per-mode deadline (AD-7) and is the only source of a `timeout` state — modes never start their own timeout timer nor throw `timeout`.

### AD-7 — Definite-state invariant; empty ≠ error

- **Binds:** all modes, `finderStateView` (NFR2, M3)
- **Prevents:** indefinite spinners, blank screens, and "found nothing" being confused with "couldn't run".
- **Rule:** Every search resolves to exactly one `StateResult` ∈ `{ results, empty, timeout, error, offline }` within its budget (core 10s; FR14 15s). Timeouts and errors always offer Retry or a fallback. **A provider signals zero matches by returning `[]` (→ `empty`), never by throwing** — a thrown `AppError` always means the search could not complete. The orchestrator maps `[]`→`empty`, deadline expiry→`timeout`, and `AppError` by kind (AD-11).

### AD-8 — Navigation to standard record page only `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** CAP-6
- **Prevents:** reinventing record detail; two owners of the detail surface.
- **Rule:** Result selection navigates via `NavigationMixin` to the standard equipment record page. The component owns **find**, never **detail**.

### AD-9 — FR14 is an isolated, online-only, pluggable provider

- **Binds:** FR14
- **Prevents:** vision-service coupling into the offline/core path; high swap cost.
- **Rule:** Snap/Describe implements `ResultProvider` like any mode but is **online-only** (feature-detected off when offline), carries its own 15s budget, and returns `confidence`-scored results. No core or offline path may depend on it. The concrete vision service sits behind the provider and is replaceable without touching core.

### AD-10 — Unidirectional state ownership

- **Binds:** orchestrator, all subcomponents
- **Prevents:** two owners of component state.
- **Rule:** Providers and infra adapters are read-only (return data / throw `AppError`). The `assetFinder` orchestrator owns all reactive state. Mode/result subcomponents are presentational: props down, events up. No child mutates shared state or calls a provider directly.

### AD-11 — Single degraded-state renderer, disjoint typed errors

- **Binds:** all modes (FR8, NFR7)
- **Prevents:** inconsistent or raw error UI; PII/existence leaks; overlapping error kinds.
- **Rule:** Providers throw typed `AppError { kind, userMessage, cause? }`; only `userMessage` reaches the DOM; the orchestrator maps `kind` to a `StateResult`; `finderStateView` renders every degraded state. The kinds are **disjoint** (no scenario maps to two): `offline` = network unavailable; `not-cached` = offline and the record isn't in the LDS cache; `no-access` = platform denied record/field visibility (record-level or FLS); `capability` = the required device capability is off/denied (scanner/GPS/camera); `api` = any other service/parse fault. There is **no `no-match` kind** (zero matches is `[]`, AD-7) and **no separate `permission` kind** (device permission → `capability`, data permission → `no-access`). `no-access`/`not-cached` never leak record existence or fields.

### AD-12 — Access control is the platform's job; the component never re-implements it

- **Binds:** all modes (NFR7)
- **Prevents:** two owners of authorization; client-side existence checks that leak or diverge.
- **Rule:** Record- and field-level access is enforced by Salesforce/LDS through the `graphqlData` layer, which returns only permitted records/fields. The component **never** adds client-side access checks or filters — it trusts the API surface. A record absent from a result set is indistinguishable from non-existence by design; an explicitly-denied fetch surfaces as `AppError(kind: no-access)` (AD-11). Locale/timezone formatting and microcopy are the only edge-side transforms; no record data is logged.

# Multi-Modal Asset Finder for Field Workers

## Why

Field technicians in large sites and remote locations need to find the correct Salesforce equipment record quickly, but mobile list views are difficult to search and may be unusable offline. A focused asset finder reduces scrolling, mistyped searches, office lookups, and duplicate asset recreation by making the technician's common lookup paths available in one place.

## Capabilities

- **CAP-1**
  - **intent:** A field technician can search equipment by name or identifier and receive typeahead results while entering the query.
  - **success:** A valid partial name or identifier produces matching equipment results without requiring a separate search submission.

- **CAP-2**
  - **intent:** A field technician can find equipment near the device's current location within a selected radius.
  - **success:** The component returns nearby equipment ranked by distance, displays distance in the user's configured metric or imperial unit, and refreshes when the selected radius changes without a page reload.

- **CAP-3**
  - **intent:** A field technician can scan a barcode or QR code on a physical equipment label to resolve the matching record.
  - **success:** A supported scan value resolves to the correct equipment record, or a meaningful user-facing error explains that resolution failed.

- **CAP-4**
  - **intent:** A technician can select a recently viewed equipment record immediately when the component opens without a search query.
  - **success:** The initial view shows the technician's recently viewed equipment records and supports selecting one without entering additional search input.

- **CAP-5**
  - **intent:** A technician can find equipment from records pre-loaded for offline use when network connectivity is unavailable.
  - **success:** Offline use returns cached results or a meaningful empty/error state; it never produces a crash or blank screen.

- **CAP-6**
  - **intent:** A technician can open the standard equipment record detail page from a result returned by any search mode.
  - **success:** Selecting a text, nearby, scan, or recent-record result navigates to the standard Salesforce equipment record page.

- **CAP-7** (FR14)
  - **intent:** A field technician can find equipment by snapping a photo or typing a freeform description when they don't know the name, identifier, or barcode.
  - **success:** With connectivity, an image or description returns candidate equipment ranked by confidence; offline, the mode is clearly presented as unavailable rather than failing silently.

## Constraints

- The solution is a focused Salesforce Lightning Web Component replacing the default equipment list view in the Salesforce mobile app, while remaining demonstrable in a desktop browser.
- All record retrieval must use the offline-capable data API; Apex must not be called at runtime.
- The mobile experience must support text/typeahead search, nearby GPS search, and barcode/QR scanning.
- Nearby search must provide at least three radius choices, update reactively, rank by distance, and respect the user's metric or imperial unit preference.
- Error and empty states must show meaningful user-facing messages rather than raw error objects.
- Degraded, empty, and failure states must be distinct across all modes: offline, record-not-cached, no-access, capability-unavailable (camera/GPS off), and no-match each get their own user-facing message. The rendering mechanism is owned by the adopted architecture spine (AD-7, AD-11).
- Image/description search (CAP-7) is online-only and isolated behind the shared result provider: it is excluded from the offline path and must not block or degrade the core find modes (architecture AD-9).
- Desktop rendering must complete without JavaScript errors and must degrade gracefully when mobile camera or location capabilities are unavailable.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning or replacing the standard equipment record detail page.
- Runtime Apex retrieval.
- Migrating assets across storage systems or normalizing the organization's tagging and metadata.
- Building a general-purpose asset management interface beyond the focused equipment lookup workflow.

## Success signal

### Title
**FieldPulse — Multi-Modal Asset Finder for Field Workers (PS-02)**

### Industry / Vertical
Field Service / Manufacturing & Utilities — Field Service Management & Digital Asset Management (primary persona: mobile Field Technician)

### Salesforce & 3rd Party stack
- Lightning Web Components (Salesforce Mobile App + desktop), API 67.0 / Summer '26
- Lightning Data Service + `lightning/uiGraphQLApi` (GraphQL wire adapters — **no runtime Apex**)
- Salesforce Mobile Offline / Briefcase Builder (Account-scoped pre-cache)
- `lightning/mobileCapabilities` — BarcodeScanner
- `lightning/navigation` NavigationMixin; standard **Asset** object (no custom object)
- Custom Metadata Type for config; Permission Set; custom mobile tab
- Browser APIs: `navigator.geolocation`, Web Speech API (voice dictation)
- Roadmap: Data Cloud (ingestion + Identity Resolution + Data Action upsert) for cross-system asset consolidation

### Client Pain Points
- Technicians scroll long mobile Asset list views — the default list view isn't built for on-site search.
- List views are unusable offline; large sites, basements and remote locations have no signal.
- Mistyped or partial serial numbers mean repeated failed searches and rework.
- Technicians phone back-office/dispatch to read a serial off a label, burning time on both sides.
- Asset metadata is inconsistently tagged, so staff recreate records that already exist (duplicates).
- Unlabeled or damaged equipment can't be identified at all from name, ID or barcode.
- Equipment data lives in more than one system, so Salesforce is never the single source of truth.

### Listen out for…. (Signals)
- *"My techs spend the first ten minutes on site just finding the right record."*
- *"The mobile app is useless once they're inside the plant — no signal."*
- *"They call the office to read a serial number off the label."*
- *"We keep finding duplicate asset records."*
- *"Half our assets don't have a readable label anymore."*
- *"Nobody knows what equipment is actually on that site."*
- *"Our asset data is split between Salesforce and \<legacy/ERP/CMMS system\>."*
- *"Every tweak to the mobile experience turns into an Apex project."*

One focused Lightning Web Component replaces the default mobile Asset list view and gets a technician to the right equipment record in **under 10 seconds** — via recently viewed (zero input), text typeahead, GPS proximity with a reactive radius, barcode/QR scan, or voice dictation.
